samples.summary: Design-doc update files the new merge/paste rules as ~40 lines of narrative inside the copy/paste bullet under Proposal Details, while the task's own Decision says the external-paste policy is "noted as a Non-Goal in sheet.md" (docs/tasks/active/20260912-sheets-paste-merge-propagation-todo.md:40). sheet.md has a real `### Non-Goals` section (line 24) and a `### Merged Cell Model` section (line 267) that already states the merge invariants — the new freeze/refusal/anchor-normalization rules belong there, folded into the canonical sections, rather than appended as prose to one bullet. Behavior is unaffected; the cost is doc discipline/findability.

The change newly enforces "a merged block may not straddle a freeze boundary" on two paths (paste via `planPasteMerges`, drag-move via the new `merge-move-frozen`), but `setFreezePane` (sheet.ts:514) sets frozenRows/frozenCols with no merge check, and the row/column shift path adjusts the freeze line without one either. The invariant is stated unconditionally in the design doc ("Merges that cross freeze pane boundaries are disallowed", sheet.md:277) and now in the new prose, yet a user can still create a straddling block by freezing, after which the block can no longer be moved or pasted — an enforcement asymmetry the doc does not record. The todo explicitly lists this as "not taken"; cost stays inside consistency of the invariant.
searchedFor: read sheet.md Merged Cell Model + Freeze Panes sections

samples.summary: Issue scope item 3 asks to "report every refusal through the #939 notice channel (`Sheet.setOnRefusal` → `Spreadsheet.onNotice`) instead of returning in silence". `paste` still returns silently when `this.pivotDefinition` is set (sheet.ts:2217) and when neither text nor html is present, so a paste onto a pivot sheet still does nothing with no notice. Arguably the scope item meant only the merge refusals, hence low confidence.

`rangeOf` is now the shared bounding-box helper (good reuse per scope item 2), but its contract for an empty grid is still undefined — it returns Infinity/-Infinity bounds and neither the doc comment nor the new tests state that callers must guard (`selectPastedRange` does). Documenting the precondition on the shared helper would keep the reuse safe as more callers adopt it.
